prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a site that (A) shows real on‑chain numbers (e.g., realized profits/losses, exchange flows) or (B) a site whose authors publish their own trading P&L (including losses)? I can recommend different things depending on which you mean — quick summary below.

If you mean on‑chain / market numbers (most common)
- Glassnode — best single resource for plain‑English explanations paired with real on‑chain metrics (Realized Loss, Unrealized P/L, exchange inflows/outflows, etc.). They have a “Glassnode Studio” dashboard and short writeups that explain what the metrics mean and show the actual numbers/charts.
- Coin Metrics — excellent “State of the Network” reports and clear datasets; good for seeing raw network-level numbers explained in simple terms.
- IntoTheBlock and CryptoQuant — user‑friendly dashboards and short explanations of the same kinds of metrics.
How to use them: For a beginner, read a short primer (CoinMarketCap/CoinGecko “Learn” or Coin Bureau) and then look at Glassnode’s “Realized Loss” and “Unrealized P/L” charts to see actual historical losses/profits.

If you mean publishers showing their own trading performance (authors publishing their own losses)
- That is much rarer and less standardized. Some independent bloggers/traders and newsletters sometimes post transparent P&L threads (look for individual traders on Twitter/X or Substack who explicitly publish audited performance), but there isn’t a single widely used beginner site that consistently posts its own loss/gain ledger the way a hedge fund would.

If you want one practical recommendation to start now
- Pair Coin Bureau (plain‑English beginner education) with Glassnode (real numbers / realized losses). Coin Bureau explains concepts clearly; Glassnode shows the actual metrics and charts.

Tell me which interpretation you meant (A or B) and your skill level/interests (DeFi, Bitcoin, NFTs, trading), and I’ll give a short step‑by‑step reading plan and specific charts/articles to look at.
